question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution directs the State for promotion of cottage industries in rural areas? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 41
Article 36
Article 55
Article 43
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 43

Explanation:
Part IV of the Indian Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). Article 43 directs the State to promote cottage industries in rural areas on an individual or cooperative basis. This article is based on Gandhian principles and focuses on strengthening the rural economy and creating employment. Other options: Article 41 deals with the right to work, education, and public assistance; Article 36 defines the State; Article 55 relates to the election of the President.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 43 → Directs promotion of cottage industries in rural areas.
☛ Article 43A → Ensures workers' participation in management of industries.
☛ Article 43B → Promotes voluntary formation of cooperative societies.
☛ Gandhian principles → Reflected in Articles 40, 43, 46, and 48.
☛ Rural development → Article 43 emphasizes rural development and employment generation.
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद राज्य को ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में कुटीर उद्योगों को बढ़ावा देने का निर्देश देता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)

अनुच्छेद 36
अनुच्छेद 55
अनुच्छेद 43
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 43

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (DPSP) शामिल हैं। अनुच्छेद 43 राज्य को निर्देश देता है कि वह ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में कुटीर उद्योगों को व्यक्तिगत या सहकारी आधार पर बढ़ावा देने का प्रयास करे। यह अनुच्छेद गांधीवादी सिद्धांतों पर आधारित है और ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूत करने तथा रोजगार सृजन पर केंद्रित है। अन्य विकल्प: अनुच्छेद 41 कार्य, शिक्षा और सार्वजनिक सहायता के अधिकार से संबंधित है; अनुच्छेद 36 राज्य की परिभाषा देता है; अनुच्छेद 55 राष्ट्रपति के चुनाव से संबंधित है।

question: Which organisation unveiled the strategic report titled 'Designing a Policy for Medium Enterprises' emphasising their role in India’s development? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Reserve Bank of India
Ministry of MSME
Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)
NITI Aayog
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is NITI Aayog

Explanation:
The strategic report titled 'Designing a Policy for Medium Enterprises' was unveiled by NITI Aayog, emphasising the need for a dedicated policy framework for medium enterprises. According to the report, medium enterprises significantly contribute to India's GDP, exports, and employment, yet lack a specific policy. It recommends a three-pillar approach focusing on capital, market access, and capacity building. The report also suggests clarifying the definition of medium enterprises, improving financial access, and providing export incentives. NITI Aayog has linked this report to the vision of 'Viksit Bharat 2047'.

question_hi: किस संगठन ने 'मध्यम उद्यमों के लिए नीति तैयार करना' नामक रणनीतिक रिपोर्ट का अनावरण किया, जिसमें भारत के विकास में उनकी भूमिका पर जोर दिया गया है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)

Solution: सही उत्तर है नीति आयोग

Explanation:

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 368
Article 240
Article 280
Article 246
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 246

Explanation:
Article 246 of the Indian Constitution deals with the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States. It provides for three lists under the Seventh Schedule: the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on Union List subjects, state legislatures on State List subjects, and both can legislate on Concurrent List subjects. This forms the core of India's federal structure. Article 368 deals with constitutional amendments, Article 240 with Union Territories, and Article 280 with the Finance Commission.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article deals with distribution of legislative powers? → Article 246
☛ Which Schedule contains the three lists? → Seventh Schedule
☛ How many subjects are in the Union List? → 100 (originally 97)
☛ Who can legislate on Concurrent List? → Both Parliament and State Legislatures
☛ Article 246 is related to? → Distribution of powers between Union and States
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद संघ और राज्यों के बीच विधायी शक्तियों के वितरण से संबंधित है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)

question: Who organises Lok Adalats in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Bar Council of India
National and State Legal Services Authorities
Law Commission of India
Advocate General of State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National and State Legal Services Authorities

Explanation:
Lok Adalats are organised by the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and State Legal Services Authorities (SLSA). These are constitutional bodies that provide free legal aid and organise Lok Adalats for the speedy disposal of disputes. Lok Adalats work on the principle of conciliation and compromise, where parties mutually agree to settle the dispute. The decisions given in Lok Adalats are final and binding on the parties. They were established under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who organises Lok Adalats? → National and State Legal Services Authorities
☛ What is the main principle of Lok Adalats? → Conciliation and compromise
☛ Under which act were Lok Adalats established? → Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
☛ Full form of NALSA? → National Legal Services Authority
☛ What is the nature of Lok Adalat decisions? → Final and binding

Explanation:

question: What is the primary purpose of Judicial Review in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: To examine the constitutionality of laws
To amend the Constitution
To appoint ministers
To elect judges
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To examine the constitutionality of laws

Explanation:
The primary purpose of Judicial Review in India is to ensure that all laws and executive orders are in conformity with the Constitution. This power is vested in the Supreme Court and High Courts, which can declare any law unconstitutional if it violates the basic structure of the Constitution. Through judicial review, the fundamental rights of citizens are protected and the powers of the government are checked. It is an integral part of India's federal structure and the principle of separation of powers.

☛ Under which Article is the power of Judicial Review in India? → Article 13
☛ On which principle is Judicial Review based? → Supremacy of the Constitution
☛ What is the most famous case of Judicial Review? → Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)
☛ What can be declared unconstitutional under Judicial Review? → Parliamentary laws and executive orders

question: Within how many days must information be provided under the RTI Act for general requests? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: 30 days
20 days
60 days
15 days
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 30 days

Explanation:
Under the Right to Information Act, 2005 of India, for general requests, the public authority must provide information within 30 days from the receipt of the application by the Information Officer. If the application pertains to another department, it must be transferred within 5 days, and the 30-day rule applies from transfer. For matters concerning life and liberty, information must be given within 48 hours. In case of delay, a penalty of Rs. 250 per day can be imposed on the Information Officer.

☛ Within how many hours must information related to life and liberty be provided under RTI? → 48 hours

☛ What is the penalty per day for delay in providing information under RTI? → Rs. 250

question_hi: आरटीआई अधिनियम के तहत सामान्य अनुरोधों के लिए कितने दिनों के भीतर जानकारी प्रदान की जानी चाहिए? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: 30 दिन
20 दिन
60 दिन
15 दिन

question: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution was introduced through the 73rd Amendment. What is its significance in the context of Panchayati Raj?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: It outlines administrative powers of the Gram Sabha.
It lists subjects to be legislated by the Union government
It specifies 29 functional subjects to be devolved to Panchayats by States.
It specifies 44 functional subjects to be devolved to Panchayats by States.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It specifies 29 functional subjects to be devolved to Panchayats by States.

Explanation:
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) introduced the Eleventh Schedule, listing 29 subjects that State governments may devolve to Panchayats. These include agriculture, education, health, rural housing, drinking water, roads, poverty alleviation, small-scale industries, women and child development, social forestry, and more. This schedule grants functional authority to Panchayati Raj institutions, strengthening local governance. Under Article 243G, Panchayats are empowered to plan and implement schemes related to these 29 subjects. The Eleventh Schedule is distinct from the Union and State lists in the Seventh Schedule and pertains exclusively to Panchayats. It empowers states to transfer administrative control over these subjects to local bodies, ensuring grassroots democracy.

question: A person who migrated from Pakistan after 19 July 1948 could become an Indian citizen, only if: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: he was registered by an officer of the Dominion of India
he was a resident of Pakistan in 1948
he took an oath of allegiance
he was born in India before 1947
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is he was born in India before 1947

Explanation:
According to Article 5 of the Indian Constitution, on 26 January 1950, a person was a citizen of India if they were born in India, or either of their parents was born in India, or they had been ordinarily resident in India for 5 years. Article 6 makes special provisions for migrants from Pakistan. Those who migrated before 19 July 1948 automatically became citizens. Those migrating after that date had to register as citizens, provided they were born in India or their parents or grandparents were born in India. Thus, the correct answer is 'he was born in India before 1947'.

Article 52
solution:

Explanation:

The President is the first citizen and the head of state of the Indian Republic. question: Which of the following changes would need the approval of at least half of all State Legislatures? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 1)

Rewriting the Preamble’s text

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Amending the Emergency provisions in Part XVIII

Explanation:
According to Article 368 of the Indian Constitution, certain amendments require approval by at least half of the state legislatures in addition to a two-thirds majority in Parliament. Other options like rewriting the Preamble or changing Fundamental Rights require only a special majority in Parliament, as they do not affect the federal structure. Altering the Union List also does not require state consent. This procedure ensures protection of the federal character and involves states in significant constitutional changes.

question: Who is described as the 'permanent executive'? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 1)

The heads of government and their ministers

In the Indian political system, the executive is divided into two parts: political executive and permanent executive. The political executive includes elected ministers and heads of government, who are temporary and change with elections. Therefore, the permanent executive is considered the backbone of the administration.

question: Under which Article does the Supreme Court of India exercise original jurisdiction in cases involving the violation of Fundamental Rights? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 32
Article 136
Article 226
Article 131
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 32

Explanation:
Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of their Fundamental Rights. It is known as the 'soul of the Constitution' because it ensures effective protection of fundamental rights. Under this Article, the Supreme Court has 'original jurisdiction', meaning affected individuals can directly file a petition before it. Article 32 mentions five types of writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari). Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul of the Constitution'. Without this Article, fundamental rights would be meaningless. This right can be suspended only during a national emergency under Article 359.

question: What is the administrative jurisdiction of Central Service officers? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)

Thus, the authority and scope of Central Service officers are confined to central administration only, not extending to states or constitutional authorities.

question: Which of the following is the aim of the Directive Principles of State Policy? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution. Thus, one of the key aims of DPSP is to promote international peace and security.

question: Which of the following Acts abolished the Dyarchy at the provincial level during the colonial period in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Indian Councils Act, 1909
Charter Act of 1853
Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1919
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The system of Dyarchy was introduced at the provincial level by the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms). Under this system, provincial departments were divided into reserved (controlled by the Governor) and transferred (under ministers responsible to the legislature). This created a dual government in provinces. The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished dyarchy and introduced provincial autonomy. It established responsible government in provinces, where the council of ministers was accountable to the legislature. Thus, the 1935 Act is credited with ending dyarchy at the provincial level.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
द्वैध शासन प्रणाली भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919 (मोंटेग्यू-चेम्सफोर्ड सुधार) द्वारा प्रांतीय स्तर पर लागू की गई थी, जिसमें विभागों को आरक्षित (गवर्नर द्वारा नियंत्रित) और हस्तांतरित (मंत्रियों को सौंपे गए) में विभाजित किया गया था। इस अधिनियम ने प्रांतों में दोहरी सरकार बनाई। भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 ने द्वैध शासन को समाप्त कर प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता की शुरुआत की। इसने प्रांतों में उत्तरदायी सरकार की स्थापना की, जहां मंत्री परिषद विधानमंडल के प्रति उत्तरदायी थी। इस प्रकार, 1935 का अधिनियम द्वैध शासन को समाप्त करने के लिए उत्तरदायी था।

question: Which of the following financial powers is not vested in the Governor of a State? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: To assent to Money Bills
To administer the State Contingency Fund
Presenting the state budget to the Legislature
Approving taxes independently
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Approving taxes independently

Explanation:
The financial powers of the Governor include giving assent to Money Bills, administering the State Contingency Fund, and presenting the state budget to the Legislature. However, the Governor cannot approve taxes independently. The power to levy taxes lies with the State Legislature, and the Governor only gives assent to bills passed by it. The Governor cannot unilaterally impose or approve taxes. This power is vested in the Legislature, not in the Governor.

question: Under which article of the Constitution is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India appointed? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 324
Article 148
Article 280
Article 76
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 148

Explanation:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is appointed under Article 148 of the Constitution. CAG is an independent authority under Part V (Chapter V) of the Indian Constitution pertaining to the Union. The CAG is appointed by the President and audits all accounts of the Government of India and state governments. Article 149 defines the duties and powers of the CAG, while Article 150 pertains to the form of accounts of the Union and states. The CAG holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. Other options: Article 324 relates to the Election Commission, Article 280 to the Finance Commission, and Article 76 to the Attorney General.

question_hi: संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के तहत भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) की नियुक्ति की जाती है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 324
अनुच्छेद 148
अनुच्छेद 280

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 148

Explanation:
भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) की नियुक्ति अनुच्छेद 148 के तहत की जाती है। CAG भारतीय संविधान के भाग V (अध्याय V) में संघ के अंतर्गत एक स्वतंत्र प्राधिकरण है। CAG की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है, और यह भारत सरकार तथा राज्य सरकारों के सभी खातों का लेखा-परीक्षण करता है। अनुच्छेद 149 CAG के कर्तव्यों और शक्तियों को परिभाषित करता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 150 संघ और राज्यों के खातों के प्रारूप से संबंधित है। CAG की नियुक्ति 6 वर्ष या 65 वर्ष की आयु तक (जो भी पहले हो) की जाती है। अन्य विकल्प: अनुच्छेद 324 चुनाव आयोग, अनुच्छेद 280 वित्त आयोग, अनुच्छेद 76 महान्यायवादी से संबंधित हैं।
